descriptionChirho: The proper noun Qots (Koz), often with the definite article as Haqqots (Hakkoz), refers to the head of a priestly family appearing in the genealogical and priestly division lists of 1 Chronicles 24:10, Ezra 2:61, and Nehemiah 3:4, 3:21, 7:63. All four clusters represent the same personal/familial name with syntactic variation: definite article (ha-Qqots 'Hakkoz'), conjunctive waw (we-Qots 'and Koz'), preposition lamed with article (le-ha-Qqots 'for Haqqots'), and another articled form (ha-Qots). Transliterations confirm identity: Arabic Haqqus (هقوص), Spanish Hacoz, Korean 하꼼스/학고스, Swahili Hakosi, Hindi Hakkoz (हक्कोज/हक्कोस). Variant spellings across languages are normal for this name.
